readerTitle: The tasting went great. So why did the school never order?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (동네 베이커리의 학교 아침 간식 납품, 학부모 소통 앱의 학교 판매) · 적용 레슨: 여러 의사결정자, 챔피언 찾기
insight: 학교에 파는 일은 한 사람을 설득하는 일이 아니다. 각자 다른 위험을 지는 여러 사람의 걱정을, 그 방 안에서 대신 말해 줄 내부자의 손에 쥐여 주는 일이다.
misconception: 교장이 좋아하고 아이들이 맛있게 먹었으면 계약은 거의 된 것이다.

sources.text: SAL-02-04 (여러 의사결정자), SAL-02-05 (챔피언 찾기) 레슨의 개념을 적용
모든 인물과 상황은 설명용 가상 사례

factChecks.note: 학교의 구매 절차, 예산 주기, 식품·알레르기 규정, 학생 개인정보 규정은 나라와 지역마다 다릅니다. 카드에는 특정 법이나 절차를 적지 않고 '많은 학교에서', '확인하라' 수준으로만 썼습니다. 법률 조언으로 읽히지 않는지 검토가 필요합니다.
수치(교사 40명 사용 등)는 모두 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 통계나 연구 인용은 없습니다.

cards.title: The tasting went great. So why did the school never order?
body: Mina runs a bakery two streets from a primary school. She pitched a healthier breakfast: oat muffins and fruit cups, delivered each morning.
At the tasting, the kids cleared the trays. The principal smiled and said, "This is exactly what we need."
Three months later, no order. No reply to her last two emails.

image.label: Empty muffin trays on a school table after a tasting
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 학교 강당 테이블 위에 빈 머핀 트레이와 부스러기. 뒤쪽 창문 밖으로 시간이 흐른 듯 낙엽이 지고, 테이블 한쪽에 답장 없는 휴대폰 알림. 실제 학교 로고나 브랜드는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What should Mina do next?
body: The principal liked it. The kids loved it. Yet the deal stalled.
What's the most useful next step?

options.text: Cut the price 15% and send a new offer
options.feedback: It gives away margin before Mina knows price is the problem. If the blocker is allergies or kitchen space, a cheaper offer still stalls.

options.text: Find out who else has to agree, and what each of them worries about
options.feedback: This is **many decision makers** at work. A school's yes is rarely one person's yes, and the quiet no often comes from someone Mina never met.

options.text: Ask the principal to sign a one-term trial now
options.feedback: Asking for a decision is reasonable. But if the principal can't sign alone, pushing harder only adds awkwardness.

cards.title: Five people, five different worries.
body: Mina asked a friendly teacher how food decisions get made. The answer was longer than she expected.

breakdown.label: No complaints
breakdown.detail: Wants happy parents and no surprises

breakdown.label: Cost per child
breakdown.detail: Controls a budget set once a year

cards.callout: Mina had won the two people with the least risk on the line.
cards.softwareNote: School software has the same map with different names: a teacher who loves it, an IT lead, someone checking student data rules, and whoever holds the budget.

cards.title: Each person carries a different risk.
body: With **many decision makers**, anyone who carries risk can quietly block the deal. Nobody has to say no. They just don't say yes.
The business manager had no line in this year's budget. The kitchen manager pictured one nut allergy incident traced to an outside supplier. Neither was at the tasting.
Mina's pitch answered *is it tasty?* The open questions were *can we pay for it?* and *is it safe?*

cards.title: Who should Mina lean on inside the school?
body: Mina can't sit in the school's meetings. She needs someone inside who wants this to happen. Three people seem friendly.

options.text: The PE teacher, who keeps telling everyone how great the muffins were
options.feedback: Enthusiasm helps, but a **champion** also needs access to the people deciding. The PE teacher has neither the budget nor the food committee.

options.text: The kitchen manager, who throws away uneaten breakfasts daily and sits on the food committee
options.feedback: A true **champion**: she feels the problem, has influence, and is in the room. Win her worries first and she can answer the others'.

options.text: The parents' group chair, who complains loudly about school food
options.feedback: She has a voice, but she pushes from outside. Staff may hear the idea as criticism and dig in.

cards.title: Give her answers she can repeat.
body: A champion sells for you when you're not there. So Mina wrote a one-page plan the kitchen manager could carry into the meeting.
It answered each person's worry in one line: allergen labels on every item, delivery at 7:15 ready to serve, cost per child, a one-term trial, and a simple way to stop.

image.label: A one-page plan with one line per decision maker
image.brief: 한 장짜리 제안서 일러스트. 왼쪽에 역할 아이콘(교장, 행정실장, 조리실장, 학부모, 아이), 오른쪽에 각각의 걱정에 대한 한 줄 답변. 조리실장이 이 종이를 들고 회의실로 들어가는 장면. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Schools run on calendars and rules.
body: Many schools set budgets once a year. Miss that window and a perfect plan waits months, so ask when money gets decided.
Food safety and student data rules vary by place. Check them before promising anything.
And never go around someone. Skipping the business manager to lobby the principal can turn a slow yes into a firm no. Champions also move jobs, so keep more than one friend inside.

cards.title: Now it's a parent messaging app.
body: Your app lets teachers message parents. One teacher started a free trial, and now 40 teachers at her school use it. The school hasn't paid anything.
How do you turn this into a paid school licence?

options.text: Ask the first teacher to introduce you to the IT lead, and ask what IT needs before approving
options.feedback: It uses your **champion** to reach a **decision maker** you haven't met, and starts with their worry, not your pitch.

options.text: Email the principal your usage numbers and ask for a licence
options.feedback: Usage is strong proof. But the principal may hand it to IT, and IT's first meeting is about a tool it never approved.

options.text: Let usage keep growing until the school has to pay
options.feedback: Growth feels like leverage. But if IT finds student data in an unapproved app, it may switch it off for everyone.

cards.title: A school buys when every worried person gets an answer.
body: Two ideas did the work here. **Many decision makers:** map everyone who carries risk and what each fears. **Finding a champion:** back the insider with influence, then give them answers to repeat.
**Try it today:** pick one stalled deal. Write down every person who could quietly block it, and one worry for each.
